scenario: You are in your mid-thirties and want to buy one camera system that can still be useful when your children graduate. Money matters less than avoiding regret, and you have heard that shutters, weather seals and lens mounts wear. Treat the ten-year goal as an aspiration, not an observed outcome. The frozen shopping set contains a Pentax K-30 white body-only page at 359.49 dollars whose title says discontinued while a later field says Is Discontinued By Manufacturer No; a Pentax K-3 Mark III body page at 1,996.95 dollars; a Pentax K-1 Mark II body bundle at 1,602.05 dollars; a Nikon D7500 import-model body bundle at 1,199 dollars with USA-compatible accessories and a one-year limited seller warranty; an international-version Canon 5D Mark IV body page at 2,499 dollars; and a Canon-EF Rokinon 14mm f/2.8 lens page at 349 dollars whose seller says the sealed lens mount protects the mount gap. Frozen model context maps the K-3 Mark III to a 2021 Pentax KAF2 interchangeable-lens DSLR, the D7500 to a 2017 Nikon F-mount DSLR and the 5D Mark IV to a 2016 Canon EF full-frame DSLR. Background pages define focal-plane shutters, lens mounts, O-rings, gaskets, reliability, MTBF, spare parts and field-replaceable units. Three community pages contain only scoped posts about donating old good-condition cameras, finding vintage lenses locally and obtaining replacement laptop parts. No source gives model-specific shutter survival distributions, exact-unit shutter counts, camera-seal materials or maintenance schedules, mount-wear measurements, current regional service and parts commitments, a controlled decade comparison or a universally most durable body and lens.
target: Audit what each frozen seller, model, mechanism, reliability, repair-parts and community source can and cannot establish about a ten-year camera-system goal. Build an exact-system table that keeps seller wording, model facts, exact-unit inspection, current written service answers, reversible-trial outcomes and unresolved fields separate. Explain what a focal-plane shutter, lens mount, O-ring, gasket, reliability estimate, MTBF, spare part and field-replaceable unit do and why none of the generic definitions predicts one unit. Preserve the K-30 discontinuation conflict and the import or international-version and seller-warranty scope. Specify the exact serial, condition, shutter-count, mount, seal-surface, lens-compatibility, battery, media, firmware, region, warranty, return, parts, service-quote and actual-use checks. Include maintenance, repair scenarios, downtime and fallback in total ownership cost. Predeclare pass, fail, unresolved and stop gates. End with the lowest-total-ownership exact passing system after independent inspection and a reversible trial, or a keep, repair, rent, smaller-system or deferral outcome. Scope any conclusion to the exact units, environment, written service answers and comparison date, and do not promise decade survival or name an automatic buy-it-for-life winner.
